one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the window to 2026-11-05. (1) Ericsson Q3 2026 report on 2026-10-15 [12]: Ericsson already flagged component-cost inflation and pressure on Networks adjusted gross margin in Q3 [11], and Dell'Oro still sees 2026 RAN revenue broadly flat [10], so the read-across to Nokia Mobile Infrastructure is neutral-to-mildly negative and largely expected. (2) Nokia Q3 2026 report on 2026-10-22 [1]: Nokia pre-guided Q3 net sales +3-7% q/q and comparable OP 'largely flat' vs Q2's EUR 434m, with a 'meaningful increase in Q4' [1] [1], so the headline is pre-announced and the swing factors are AI & Cloud order intake (EUR 2.8bn in Q2, which the CEO said should not be expected every quarter [3]), MI gross margin (CFO guided closer to 44-46% [3]) and FCF tracking at the low end of 55-75% [3]. The chain is supportive (Dell'Oro optical +15% y/y and DCI +45% in 2Q26 [9]; Ciena raised its FY26 guide to +35% [13]). Today's move was sector-wide with no Nokia filing. No directional call: lognormal centred at $10.80 (brief price $10.84 (a 6 Oct intraday price from the run brief; the official 6 Oct close was $10.975, StockAnalysis NOK history)), monthly sigma 0.17 (62% annual vol / 3.5 ~ 0.177), with 20% weight on a sigma-0.30 component for the earnings-day jump risk inside the window. P(close >= $10.84) = 0.49.

fair_value.method: Blend of 65% P/E (NTM comparable EPS at Oct-2027 EUR 0.416 x 18.0x = EUR 7.49 = $8.44 at ECB 1.1269) and 35% DCF (2028 FCF EUR 2.205bn = 3.15bn OP x 70% CMD conversion, +5%/yr to 2032, 3% terminal, 9.54% discount; EV EUR 36.86bn + reported net cash EUR 2.776bn = EUR 39.64bn / 5,801.9m = EUR 6.83 = $7.70) -> 0.65 x 8.44 + 0.35 x 7.70 = $8.18 per ADS.

bear.story: AI & Cloud orders prove lumpy as the CEO warned [3] and conversion slips on supply constraints; memory/component inflation squeezes MI margins (Ericsson and Calix already flag it [11][14]) in a flat RAN market [10]; FY26 conversion stays at the low end [3]. 2028 OP at the CMD bottom end EUR 2.7bn -> EPS (2.7+0.15) x 0.735 / 5.802 = EUR 0.361; the AI premium disappears and NOK trades like the telecom/access peers at 14x (ERIC 13.75x, HLIT 14.25x, ADTN 15.0x) -> EUR 5.05 = $5.70. Below the thesis-break price.

base.story: Nokia delivers FY26 'somewhat above the midpoint' [1] and tracks the upper half of the 2028 target; NTM EPS at Oct-2027 EUR 0.416 (same as fair value). The market keeps part of today's AI-optical premium: multiple 20.5x = my 18x fair multiple plus ~40% of the current 6.5-turn gap to 24.5x (judgment: valuation gaps rarely close fully in 12 months) -> EUR 8.53 = $9.61, 17% above fair value and 11% below spot.

bull.story: Optical/DCI keeps compounding (Dell'Oro optical +15%, DCI +45% [9]; Ciena FY26 +35% [13]) and AI & Cloud backlog converts faster; 2028 OP EUR 3.55bn, above the CMD top end -> EPS (3.55+0.15) x 0.735 / 5.802 = EUR 0.469; NOK is re-rated to 28x, near Viavi's 27.7x and below Ciena/Arista (38-43x) -> EUR 13.12 = $14.79, still below the 52-week high of $17.45.

comps_summary.peer_range: NTM P/E (Oct-2026 to Sep-2027) 13.15x (RBBN) to 43.30x (ANET); median 16.18x (CALX). Basis: S&P Global 'EPS This Year'/'EPS Next Year' from each StockAnalysis forecast page, time-weighted by months to each fiscal year-end (Dec FYE 0.25/0.75; CSCO Jul FYE 10/12 current FY27; VIAV Jun FYE 9/12 current FY27; CIEN and HPE Oct FYE 1/12 FY26 + 11/12 FY27), divided by the 2026-10-06 price shown on the same page. StockAnalysis 'Forward PE' is not used because it mixes fiscal bases. Split: telecom/access cluster 13.2-16.2x (RBBN, ERIC, HLIT, ADTN, HPE, CALX); optical/IP/mission-critical cluster 22.4-43.3x (CSCO, MSI, VIAV, CIEN, ANET). Forward EV/EBITDA: no verified consensus EBITDA on a consistent forward basis was reachable (Twelve Data estimates need a paid plan; StockAnalysis shows only trailing EV/EBITDA), so EV/EBITDA is not used and the field is null. ZTE (HK 0763) and NEC (6701.T) are genuine RAN/optical peers but no verified EPS consensus was reachable (StockAnalysis 404 / no EPS), so they are excluded; Juniper and Infinera are no longer listed.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 18.0x NTM, +11% vs the 16.2x median and inside the 13.2-43.3x range. NOK itself trades at 24.5x NTM (EUR 9.62 = $10.8414/1.1269 over NTM EPS 0.25 x 0.34 + 0.75 x 0.41 = EUR 0.3925), a 51% premium to the median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The +11% premium is profit mix only, and that mix is structural through the horizon: about 47% of 2028E segment OP is Network Infrastructure (Optical, IP, Fixed), whose closest listed comparables trade at 22-43x, and Nokia is among the top four optical vendors (Huawei, Ciena, Nokia, Cisco) and co-leader in disaggregated WDM with Ciena (Dell'Oro [9]); the CMD commits to NI 6-8% sales CAGR (Optical+IP 10-12%) and 13-17% margin [2]. I value NI at Cisco's 22.35x, not the Ciena/Arista 38-43x, because NI's margin (9.9% FY25 recast [1]) and target growth match a mature IP/optical incumbent rather than a hyper-growth one. The remaining 53% (Mobile Infrastructure) gets Ericsson's 13.75x because RAN is projected flat in 2026 [10]. No premium is given for AI sentiment, the sell-side PT ($14.97 [5]) or outperformance calls.

thesis_break_reason: $6.35 = EUR 5.64 = Ericsson's 13.75x NTM multiple [16] on FY2027 consensus EUR 0.41 [5], at ECB 1.1269 [6]. At that level the market would be paying a plain RAN-vendor multiple and nothing for the optical/IP franchise or the AI & Cloud backlog. Getting there most likely means a fundamental break (AI & Cloud orders cancelled or not converting, FY26 guide cut below the EUR 2.1bn floor, or the 2028 EUR 2.7-3.2bn target abandoned), not ordinary 62%-vol noise.

reasoning: Lane: industry. The value chain still splits in two. Optical/IP is strong: Dell'Oro has optical transport +15% y/y and DCI +45% in 2Q26, with Nokia among the top four vendors (Huawei, Ciena, Nokia, Cisco) and co-leader with Ciena in disaggregated WDM [9]; Ciena's FQ3 revenue was $1.67bn vs $1.22bn and its FY26 guide is +35% [13]. That fits Nokia's AI & Cloud sales +103% and EUR 2.8bn Q2 orders [1]. Mobile is flat: Dell'Oro sees 2026 RAN broadly flat [10], Ericsson's organic sales fell 1% with component inflation and Q3 Networks margin pressure [11], and Calix lost 240bp of gross margin to memory costs [14]. Round-2 changes follow the supervisor's checks, each re-verified at source. (a) Comps are rebuilt on one NTM basis across 11 peers (median 16.2x, not my round-1 mixed-basis 20.8x). GLW (materials) and EXTR (enterprise campus) are dropped; VIAV and HLIT are added; MSI and RBBN are kept on the corrected basis. (b) The multiple is now 18x, from an explicit mix: 47% NI at Cisco's 22.35x and 53% MI at Ericsson's 13.75x. I disagree with the supervisor's 20x because it values NI at ~26x off a CIEN/ANET/CSCO median, while NI's 9.9% margin and 6-8% growth target look like Cisco's, not Ciena's or Arista's. (c) Net cash is the reported EUR 2,776m, not my unverified EUR 4.3bn build. (d) FX is ECB 1.1269 and the 10Y is 5.31% on 10/05. Fair value is $8.18 (P/E $8.44, DCF $7.70), 25% below the $10.84 brief price (a 6 Oct intraday price from the run brief; the official 6 Oct close was $10.975, StockAnalysis NOK history). NOK trades at 24.5x NTM, and the gap is AI-optical sentiment that moves with Ciena and Arista; I expect it to narrow but not close within 12 months. Scenarios are bear $5.70 (25%), base $9.61 (50%) and bull $14.79 (25%), with a mean of $9.93. The bear and bull are built from the CMD target ends and peer clusters; the base is fair-value EPS at 20.5x. The ladder is a 50/50 blend of (i) a mixture of lognormals at the three scenario prices (sigma 0.25-0.28 within each) and (ii) a single lognormal with median $9.60 and sigma 0.55, slightly below the 62% realized vol because part of that vol was the one-off AI re-rating. That gives a ladder median of about $9.56, P(>= $10.84, the brief price) = 0.395 and P(>= $6.50) = 0.78. The ladder median sits between fair value ($8.18) and spot, consistent with the base case. Limits: Twelve Data hit its per-minute credit limit, so peer prices are the 2026-10-06 intraday prices printed on each StockAnalysis forecast page next to the EPS used. No verified forward EV/EBITDA or FY2028 consensus was available.
